findings.title: Client-side upload size validation hardcoded to 10MB, ignoring site settings
findings.body: validateUploadedFile previously read the limit from Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb'], which distinguishes max_image_size_kb from max_attachment_size_kb and respects admin configuration. The change replaces it with a hardcoded 10 * 1024. Consequences: sites that set a lower limit (e.g., 1MB images) will no longer block oversized files client-side, sites that set a higher limit will now wrongly reject valid uploads, attachments are incorrectly capped by the image-size logic, and the 'file too large' error message reports a max_size_kb that has no relation to the configured value.

findings.title: 413 error handler reports a hardcoded 10MB limit instead of the configured max image size
findings.body: displayErrorForUpload used to show Discourse.SiteSettings.max_image_size_kb in the file_too_large message when the web server returns 413. It now shows a hardcoded 10MB, so users are told the wrong maximum whenever the admin has configured max_image_size_kb to anything else, making the error message misleading.

findings.title: URL download limit hardcoded to 10MB, breaking API uploads for other limits and non-image files
findings.body: FileHelper.download for API-provided URLs previously used SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb.kilobytes as the cap; it is now hardcoded to 10.megabytes. This download path is used for any file type, not just images, so attachment downloads via the API are now silently capped at 10MB regardless of max_attachment_size_kb, and sites with max_image_size_kb set above 10MB cannot fetch larger images even though the downsizing logic below was intended to shrink them.

findings.title: Duplicate definition of OptimizedImage.downsize makes the width/height overload unreachable
findings.body: The class now defines self.downsize twice: once as downsize(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts) at line 145 and again as downsize(from, to, dimensions, opts) at line 149. In Ruby the second definition silently replaces the first, so the four-argument form is dead code. Any existing or future caller that passes max_width and max_height (the established API of this method) will now raise ArgumentError: wrong number of arguments (4 for 3). The two-APIs-in-one-method approach needs a different mechanism (e.g., a separate method name or a single signature).

findings.title: Animated GIF path passes "80%" to gifsicle --resize-fit, which does not accept percentages
findings.body: The new upload-downsizing code calls OptimizedImage.downsize(..., "80%", allow_animation: SiteSetting.allow_animated_thumbnails). For GIFs with allow_animation set, optimize dispatches to downsize_instructions_animated, which delegates to resize_instructions_animated and emits `gifsicle ... --resize-fit 80%`. gifsicle's --resize-fit expects a WIDTHxHEIGHT geometry, not a percentage, so the command fails, convert_with returns false, and the controller's retry loop runs 5 times without shrinking the file. The result: animated GIFs larger than max_image_size_kb always fail to upload instead of being downsized, and the loop silently wastes 5 shell-outs before giving up.

findings.title: Downsize retry loop ignores failure and silently gives up after 5 attempts
findings.body: The while loop never checks the boolean returned by OptimizedImage.downsize. If conversion fails (corrupt image, missing delegate, gifsicle geometry error), the loop burns all 5 attempts shelling out to a command that cannot succeed, then proceeds to Upload.create_for with the original oversized file, which then fails validation with a generic size error. A failed downsize should break out immediately (or surface a meaningful error) rather than retrying an unchanged file.
